calls.prompt:
Company: Brightside Foods Co.

US mid-size packaged food company (~900 employees, plants in Ohio and Georgia). Makes hot dogs and sausages, brightly colored gummy candy, and pecan-and-apple snack bars. Buys pecans, apples and corn from US farms. Sells through grocery chains and convenience stores (many customers pay with SNAP / food stamps). Runs its own fleet of 40 delivery trucks. No restaurants, no alcohol, no exports.

Rules that APPLY:
- FDA food additive and color additive rules (dyes in candy, casings, meat)
- Food labeling and food safety rules for packaged food and meat products
- EPA pesticide residue limits on crops we buy (pecans, apples, corn)
- USDA marketing orders and grading for pecans and apples
- SNAP rules that change what shoppers can buy or who qualifies (affects demand)
- Workplace safety and labor rules for food plants; trucking safety rules for our fleet

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Aviation, airspace, aircraft airworthiness
- Banking, securities, crypto, sanctions
- Medicare/Medicaid payment rules, medical devices
- Mining, offshore oil and gas, fisheries
- Broadcast/TV licensing

Affected areas and owners:
- food-safety: Additives, dyes, labeling, food safety → Maria Chen (Food Safety & Regulatory)
- sourcing: Ingredients from farms, pesticide limits, crop rules → Tom Alvarez (Sourcing)
- sales: Retail channels, SNAP, pricing → Aisha Grant (Sales Compliance)
- operations: Plant safety, labor, trucking fleet → Ben Kowalski (Operations)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-23 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if it is a rule or proposed rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-10-23, or a final rule that took effect within the 30 days before 2026-10-23; otherwise High for final rules, Medium for proposed rules and for notices with a deadline, Low for anything else), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.
calls.output:
I found three Federal Register documents in the 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-23 window that affect Brightside. My searches weren't an exhaustive scan of every document published that week, so treat the list as incomplete.

**1. 2026-21658 — Critical**
- **Title:** Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Electronic Benefits Transfer Card Security Measures
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21658/supplemental-nutrition-assistance-program-electronic-benefits-transfer-card-security-measures
- **Type and date:** A proposed rule by the Food and Nutrition Administration, published 10/23/2026.
- **Key deadline:** Written comments are due on or before December 22, 2026. That is under 90 days after 10/23, so it is Critical.
- **Owner:** sales, Aisha Grant
- **Reason:** The rule would modernize EBT technology and align it with consumer payment industry standards. It changes how SNAP shoppers and the grocery and convenience retailers who buy from us handle benefits, which could affect demand. It is not a rule that applies to us directly.
- **Action:** Ask key retail customers how they will handle the changes, and decide whether to file comments through a trade association by 12/22/2026.

**2. 2026-21669 — Medium**
- **Title:** Hazard Analysis and Risk-Based Preventive Controls for Human Food
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-21669
- **Type and date:** This was filed for public inspection on 10/22/2026 under FDA "Proposed Rules," scheduled for publication 10/23/2026. The 10/23 Federal Register lists it under Proposed Rules, docket FDA-2016-D-2343. The text appears to be draft guidance rather than a rule.
- **Key deadline:** I could not confirm a specific comment date. The docket text says comments on any guidance can be submitted at any time. Check the document for a date by which FDA wants comments on the draft.
- **Tier:** Medium. It is a proposed-rule-section item with no confirmed deadline, so it does not meet the Critical test.
- **Owner:** food-safety, Maria Chen
- **Reason:** It covers FDA's preventive-controls (food safety plan) requirements, which apply to our gummy candy and snack bar plants in Ohio and Georgia. Our hot dogs and sausages are under USDA FSIS instead.
- **Action:** Maria's team should read the draft, compare it with our current food safety plans, and set a comment date.

**3. 2026-21390 — Medium**
- **Title:** Parts and Accessories Necessary for Safe Operation; Application for an Exemption From Grote Industries, LLC
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-21390
- **Type and date:** A notice published 10/20/2026. It gives new information on Grote's request for an exemption from the steady-burning lamp requirement for commercial vehicles. If granted, carriers could run vehicles with auxiliary warning lamps controlled by Grote's Rear-End Collision Warning system.
- **Key deadline:** The comment period is reopened through Nov. 19, 2026.
- **Owner:** operations, Ben Kowalski
- **Reason:** It could change which rear warning lighting is allowed on trucks like our 40-truck delivery fleet. It is optional and does not require us to do anything.
- **Action:** Ben should decide whether the fleet wants this lighting and comment by 11/19/2026 if so. No compliance change is needed now.

**Leads without a document number**
I saw these in search results but could not get a document number, so I left them out:
- An FMCSA information-collection notice on entry-level CMV driver training certification, dated 10/21.
- An item on the AFDO Federal Register update for 10/21–22 that asks FDA to review herbicides used as preharvest desiccants, including tolerance levels.

I excluded the other FDA documents from the window because they don't apply to us:
- Cadmium action levels for baby food.
- Export certificates. We have no exports.
- Product jurisdiction and combination products.
- Cosmetics recalls.

I also found nothing in the window from EPA on pesticide tolerances for pecans, apples or corn, from USDA AMS on pecan or apple orders, or from OSHA. The pecan marketing order proposed rule I did find was published 11/9/2026, which is outside the window.
